events.title: Edison Patents the Incandescent Lamp
events.description: Thomas Edison filed a patent for his electric incandescent lamp. The filing covered the design that helped bring practical electric lighting into homes and businesses.
events.significance: Affordable electric light changed how people worked, studied and lived after dark, and it helped launch the age of electrification.

events.title: Baird Demonstrates Television
events.description: Scottish inventor John Logie Baird gave the first public demonstration of a working television system in London. He showed moving images transmitted as electrical signals.
events.significance: The demonstration was an early step toward television, which became one of the most influential communication media of the 20th century.

events.title: Auschwitz Is Liberated
events.description: Soviet Red Army troops entered the Auschwitz concentration camp complex and freed about 7,000 prisoners the Nazis had left behind. Auschwitz was the largest Nazi death camp.
events.significance: The date is now observed as International Holocaust Remembrance Day, when the world honors the millions of victims of the Holocaust and renews its commitment to fighting hatred.

events.title: Apollo 1 Fire Kills Three Astronauts
events.description: Gus Grissom, Edward White and Roger Chaffee died in a fire inside their Apollo 1 spacecraft. It broke out during a launch rehearsal test at Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
events.significance: The tragedy led to major safety redesigns of the spacecraft. Those changes helped make the later Apollo missions to the Moon possible.
